adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent the new logic is:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the only case where the `find` runs), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, so it will almost always return no match and `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined`. That value is then used as the `calendarId` for `calendar.events.update(...)` (no fallback is shown here like in createEvent’s `|| "primary"`). This is a correctness bug introduced by the diff: updates/reschedules without a stored `externalCalendarId` will fail instead of targeting the intended destination calendar (likely the first/credential-matched destination calendar).

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent the new logic is:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined, the fallback branch runs but still compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined`), which will almost never match a real destination calendar. That makes `calendarId` undefined and the code will fall back to `defaultCalendarId` ("primary") for the delete call, whereas previously it would use `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. This is a real, verifiable correctness regression introduced by the diff.
